In 2010, we had an election and it was a wave election. It was when the Tea Party came in and it was at a time my kids weren't in high school. And I looked at what was happening around the country and saw that we faced some pretty significant challenges, challenges of the economy. You run down the list of challenges we face as a country. And what I saw in this new Tea Party Congress that came in 2011 was not a willingness to work together and get things done to move our country forward, but a sense of obstruction and fighting each other. And my son, my oldest son was a senior in high school, my youngest son was a sophomore, and I looked at them and I looked at their generation and said, if we're going to give our kids the future they deserve, we have to start working together to solve the problems and pursue the opportunities we have as a nation. And that's really what got me thinking about doing something. I mentioned a couple weeks ago. I was home for a week, which was a wonderful experience. Prior to that in-district work period, as we call it, we had surveyed our constituents. I'd sent out an email to people asking, what matters to you? And we got literally thousands of responses. So we arranged to have essentially a session on each one of those issues. We started with a session on climate change in Fox Lake. talked about the impact of climate change and the potential possible responses at both the local, state and federal level. Fox Lake faces flooding threats, not just from the rains falling on Fox Lake, but the waters coming down from Lake Michigan. I had a standing room only crowd and a great conversation. The second issue we talked about was healthcare, had an event at Oakton Community College. And again, we're seeing healthcare where the price of prescription drugs are rising faster than inflation. We had a wonderful session on gun violence here in Deerfield, people on all sides of the issue, but again, talking about discourse, we had people on opposite sides of an issue willing to talk and listen to each other and speak with respect, and that was fantastic.
